title: Microsoft Purview: retention policies to delete Microsoft Teams call logs
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, PowerShell controls and permissions path match Microsoft's documentation. The page correctly explains the separate policy's limited reach, deletion delays and hold exceptions, and distinguishes general retention licensing from unpublished call-log-specific entitlements.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The roadmap describes countries' maximum calling-log retention requirements and a compliance gap from indefinite retention.
claims.quote: regulatory requirements in various countries specify maximum retention periods for calling-related logs. This discrepancy creates a compliance gap, as the existing retention practices may not meet regulatory obligations.

claims.claim: The roadmap also mentions administrators preferring to retain data longer.
claims.quote: Additionally, tenant administrators may prefer to retain data for longer periods to improve the user experience.

claims.claim: Purview supports a separate retention policy to delete Teams call logs.
claims.quote: the following command creates a delete-only rule that permanently deletes Teams call log data after one year:

claims.claim: Teams call logs include call data records, also called call detail records, and other call metadata generated by Teams.
claims.quote: Microsoft Teams call logs represent the collection of call-related data generated by Teams, including call data records (CDRs, sometimes also known as call detail records or just call records) and other call metadata.

claims.claim: Call-log data can be stored in multiple underlying Teams locations but targeted as one retention workload.
claims.quote: This data can be stored across multiple underlying locations used by Teams, but can be targeted as a single workload for retention purposes.

claims.claim: Learn points to personal call logs as an example.
claims.quote: Personal call logs - View your call history in Microsoft Teams

claims.claim: Learn points to shared call queue logs as an example.
claims.quote: Shared call queue logs - View call history in the Queues app in Microsoft Teams

claims.claim: Deletion is the only applicable retention action for Teams call logs.
claims.quote: The deletion flow and process is the same as for Teams messages, only simplified because the call-related records in call logs can't be edited or deleted by users, and because deletion is the only applicable action.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: By default Teams call logs are retained indefinitely, including uncovered new records.
claims.quote: By default, Teams call logs are retained indefinitely. Use a retention policy for call logs if you need to delete this data for compliance reasons.

claims.claim: The new retention control is admin-opt-in: an administrator must configure a call-log policy for deletion.
claims.quote: By default, Teams call logs are retained indefinitely. Use a retention policy for call logs if you need to delete this data for compliance reasons.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Scope: Tooling; Governance controls
claims.claim: The call-log policy can be created and modified only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: This separate retention policy for call logs can be created and modified only by using PowerShell.

claims.where: controls[0].note; What's changing; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: The created policy is visible but read-only in the Microsoft Purview portal.
claims.quote: After you create the retention policy for Teams call logs, it's displayed in Data Lifecycle Management > Policies in the Microsoft Purview portal, where it's visible but read-only.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The portal route to view the read-only policy is Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Policies.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Policies > Retention policies.

claims.where: controls[0].note; What's changing; Why it matters; Scope; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: The call-log policy reaches only records created after it is configured and active, leaving earlier gap records outside its reach.
claims.quote: The policy applies only to new call logs that are created after the policy is configured and active.

claims.claim: The call-log policy covers both Teams chat and Teams channel call logs.
claims.quote: The policy includes call logs for both Teams chat and Teams channels.

claims.claim: Before late April 2026, CDRs for Teams chats and channels were included in Teams chat retention policies.
claims.quote: Prior to supporting the retention of Teams call logs in late April 2026, CDRs for Teams chat and Teams channels were included in retention policies for the Teams chat location.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Since the late-April change, new CDRs require a call-log retention policy rather than a Teams chat retention policy.
claims.quote: Going forward, new CDRs are supported only when you create a retention policy for Teams call logs.

claims.claim: Earlier CDRs already covered by Teams chat policies remain managed by those policies.
claims.quote: CDRs included in previous Teams chat retention policies continue to be managed by those same policies.

claims.where: controls[0].api; What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: New-AppRetentionCompliancePolicy -Name "<PolicyName>" -Applications "User:MicrosoftTeamsCallLog" -ExchangeLocation "All" creates the call-log policy for all mailboxes, before adding its rule.
claims.quote: "User:MicrosoftTeamsCallLog"; The value All for all mailboxes. You can only use this value by itself. After you create the retention policy, use the New-AppRetentionComplianceRule cmdlet to create a retention rule

claims.where: controls[1].api; What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: New-AppRetentionComplianceRule -Name "<RuleName>" -Policy "<PolicyName>" -RetentionDuration <days> -RetentionComplianceAction Delete sets the call-log deletion rule and period in days.
claims.quote: Use the New-AppRetentionComplianceRule to create app retention compliance rules. The RetentionComplianceAction parameter specifies the retention action for the rule. Valid values are: Delete; An integer: The hold duration in days.

claims.where: controls[2].api; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance controls
claims.claim: New-AppRetentionCompliancePolicy -Name "<PolicyName>" -Applications "User:MicrosoftTeamsCallLog" -RestrictiveRetention $true enables Preservation Lock for the call-log policy.
claims.quote: "User:MicrosoftTeamsCallLog"; The RestrictiveRetention parameter specifies whether Preservation Lock is enabled for the policy. Valid values are: $true: Preservation Lock is enabled for the policy.

claims.claim: There is no documented portal UI to configure the call-log retention policy.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams call logs retention policy portal UI retention duration Preservation Lock PowerShell billing meter licensing; opened create-retention-policies and retention-policies-teams. The feature-specific instructions say PowerShell only and portal read-only.

claims.claim: There is no documented portal UI to configure the call-log deletion period.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams call logs retention duration configure Microsoft Purview portal UI; opened create-retention-policies and retention-policies-teams. The call-log policy is documented as PowerShell-only and read-only in the portal.

claims.claim: There is no documented portal UI to enable Preservation Lock.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams call logs" "Preservation Lock" "portal"; opened retention-preservation-lock, create-retention-policies and the policy cmdlet reference. Preservation Lock explicitly requires PowerShell and is not available in the UI.

claims.claim: The Purview membership path is Settings > Roles and scopes > Role groups > Role groups for Microsoft Purview solutions > role group > Edit > Edit members of the role group > Choose users.
claims.quote: Go to Settings > Roles and scopes; Select Role groups; On Role groups for Microsoft Purview solutions, select a Microsoft Purview role group ... Select Edit on the control bar. On Edit members of the role group, select Choose users or Choose groups.

claims.claim: Add-RoleGroupMember -Identity "<role-group>" -Member "<user-UPN>" adds a user to a role group.
claims.quote: Use the Add-RoleGroupMember cmdlet to add members to a management role group. The Identity parameter specifies the role group to add a member to. The Member parameter specifies who you want to add to the role group. User ID or user principal name (UPN)

claims.where: controls[3].note; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Compliance Administrator role-group members can create and manage retention policies.
claims.quote: To grant permissions for this limited administration, we recommend that you add users to the Compliance Administrator admin role group.

claims.where: controls[3].note; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: A custom role group with Retention Management is an alternative for retention-policy administration.
claims.quote: Alternatively to using this default role, you can create a new role group and add the Retention Management role to this group.

claims.claim: View-Only Retention Management provides read-only access.
claims.quote: For a read-only role, use View-Only Retention Management.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Preservation Lock cannot be undone: a locked policy can be increased or extended but not reduced, disabled or turned off.
claims.quote: A locked policy can be increased or extended, but it can't be reduced, disabled, or turned off.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: After expiry, the configured policy automatically permanently deletes eligible call-log records without a per-record approval step.
claims.quote: At the end of the retention period, the call-related record is moved to the SubstrateHolds folder. This action typically takes between 1-7 days from the expiry date. The record is retained there for at least 1 day and then permanently deleted the next time the timer job runs

claims.claim: Call-log records typically move to SubstrateHolds 1-7 days after expiry.
claims.quote: At the end of the retention period, the call-related record is moved to the SubstrateHolds folder. This action typically takes between 1-7 days from the expiry date.

claims.claim: Call-log records stay in SubstrateHolds for at least one day.
claims.quote: The record is retained there for at least 1 day

claims.claim: Eligible call-log records are permanently deleted on the next timer-job run, typically within 1-7 days.
claims.quote: then permanently deleted the next time the timer job runs (typically between 1-7 days).

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Permanent deletion is suspended while a record is subject to an applicable retaining policy or eDiscovery hold.
claims.quote: this action is suspended if the message is subject to another retention policy to retain the item or it's subject to an eDiscovery hold. Substitute "call-related record" for the word "message" and the behavior and timings remain the same.
